metadata.title: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Detailed directed graph covering ISA contracts, instruction semantics and classes, operand models, encoding, memory and exceptions, privilege, toolchains, compilers, implementation strategies, performance, representative architectures, extensions, and security facilities.

source_basis.title: Instruction set architecture
source_basis.coverage_used: Definition, compatibility, ISA versus microarchitecture, classifications, instruction types, encoding, operand counts, register pressure, instruction length, code density, design, and implementation.

source_basis.title: Supplemental architecture knowledge
source_basis.coverage_used: Expanded memory-model, toolchain, compiler, extension, virtualization, security, and implementation connections.

metadata.id_convention: Lowercase snake_case entity IDs derived from canonical names; sequential relationship IDs within this artifact.
metadata.relationship_direction: Every edge is directed from source to target; reverse edges are not implied.
metadata.scope_note: Conceptual cross-ISA knowledge graph, not a normative specification or exhaustive opcode inventory.

entities.name: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
entities.description: Abstract programmer-visible contract defining instructions, architectural state, registers, data types, addressing, memory behavior, exceptions, and system interfaces.

entities.name: Machine instruction
entities.description: Encoded operation interpreted according to the ISA, with explicit and/or implicit operands.

entities.name: Machine code
entities.description: Binary encoding of instructions and operand fields.

entities.name: Assembly language
entities.description: Symbolic representation of machine instructions, registers, operands, labels, and directives.

entities.name: Opcode
entities.description: Encoding that identifies an operation or operation family.

entities.name: Operand
entities.description: Source, destination, address, immediate value, register, memory reference, or implicit value used by an instruction.

entities.name: Instruction semantics
entities.description: Architecturally specified effects of executing an instruction, independent of implementation microarchitecture.

entities.name: Architectural state
entities.description: Program-visible state including registers, instruction pointer, status flags, control state, and memory effects.

entities.name: Program counter / instruction pointer
entities.description: State identifying the instruction stream location used for execution and control flow.

entities.name: Status register / condition codes
entities.description: State recording conditions such as zero, carry, overflow, sign, or comparison results.

entities.name: Register file
entities.description: Set of architecturally visible registers used for operands, addresses, results, and control state.

entities.name: Data type
entities.description: ISA-supported interpretation of bits, such as integer, floating-point, vector, predicate, pointer, or packed decimal.

entities.name: Addressing mode
entities.description: Rule determining how an instruction identifies an operand or computes an effective address.

entities.name: Effective address
entities.description: Computed address used to identify a memory operand.

entities.name: Immediate value
entities.description: Constant encoded directly in an instruction.

entities.name: Implicit operand
entities.description: Operand or state effect implied by opcode or execution context rather than explicitly encoded.

entities.name: Memory model
entities.description: Rules governing ordering, visibility, atomicity, and consistency of memory operations.

entities.name: Exception
entities.description: Synchronous architectural event such as a fault, trap, or abort.

entities.name: Interrupt
entities.description: Event redirecting execution to a handler, commonly from an asynchronous system condition.

entities.name: Privilege level
entities.description: Architectural execution level controlling access to privileged instructions and state.

entities.name: System call
entities.description: Controlled transition from application execution into operating-system service code.

entities.name: ABI (Application Binary Interface)
entities.description: Platform contract covering calling conventions, data layout, object formats, and system interfaces beyond the ISA alone.

entities.name: Microarchitecture
entities.description: Internal processor design implementing an ISA through pipelines, execution units, caches, prediction, and scheduling.

entities.name: ISA implementation
entities.description: Physical processor, emulator, interpreter, or translation system implementing the architectural contract.

entities.name: Binary compatibility
entities.description: Ability to execute compatible machine code across conforming implementations, subject to extensions, ABI, and OS requirements.

entities.name: Instruction extension
entities.description: Optional or later-added instruction, architectural state, or capability.

entities.name: Feature discovery
entities.description: Mechanism allowing software to discover supported ISA extensions and architectural features.

entities.name: Reserved encoding
entities.description: Bit pattern reserved by the specification, with status defined by architecture.

entities.name: Instruction decoder
entities.description: Logic identifying instruction boundaries and decoding operation fields.

entities.name: Execution unit
entities.description: Resource performing integer, floating-point, vector, address, or specialized operations.

entities.name: Micro-operation (uop)
entities.description: Internal implementation-level operation into which an instruction may be decomposed.

entities.name: Microcode
entities.description: Internal control sequence used by some processors to implement complex instructions.

entities.name: Instruction set simulator
entities.description: Software model simulating architectural instruction behavior.

entities.name: Emulator
entities.description: Software or hardware system reproducing an ISA or platform sufficiently to run programs.

entities.name: Interpreter
entities.description: Repeatedly decodes and executes instruction representations.

entities.name: Dynamic binary translation
entities.description: Runtime translation of machine-code blocks between execution models or ISAs.

entities.name: JIT compilation
entities.description: Compilation of bytecode or intermediate representation into executable code at runtime.

entities.name: CISC
entities.description: Complex instruction set design style with rich instruction forms or addressing modes.

entities.name: RISC
entities.description: Reduced instruction set design style emphasizing simpler operations and often load/store organization.

entities.name: VLIW
entities.description: Wide instruction word encoding multiple operations, often scheduled by compiler.

entities.name: LIW
entities.description: Long instruction word family related to VLIW.

entities.name: EPIC
entities.description: Explicitly parallel instruction computing exposing parallelism and scheduling responsibility to compiler/software.

entities.name: MISC
entities.description: Minimal instruction set computer approach, often using a small stack-oriented instruction set.

entities.name: OISC
entities.description: One-instruction set computer model where one primitive instruction can express general computation.

entities.name: Load-store architecture
entities.description: Ordinary arithmetic uses registers; memory access uses explicit load/store instructions.

entities.name: Stack machine
entities.description: Arithmetic commonly consumes operands from an evaluation stack.

entities.name: Accumulator machine
entities.description: Uses an implicit accumulator as a common source and/or destination.

entities.name: Register-register architecture
entities.description: Arithmetic and logic generally use register operands and register results.

entities.name: Register-memory architecture
entities.description: Instruction forms allow memory operands directly in operations.

entities.name: Memory-memory architecture
entities.description: Instruction forms operate directly on multiple memory operands.

entities.name: Transport-triggered architecture (TTA)
entities.description: Operand transport triggers operations; designs may lack conventional opcode fields.

entities.name: Bytecode ISA
entities.description: Virtual instruction set interpreted or compiled by a runtime.

entities.name: Native ISA
entities.description: Machine instruction set implemented by hardware or a close compatible execution engine.

entities.name: Zero-operand instruction form
entities.description: Arithmetic uses implicit stack operands; stack access instructions may still have operands.

entities.name: One-operand instruction form
entities.description: One explicit operand with other operands/results implicit, often accumulator-based.

entities.name: Two-operand instruction form
entities.description: Two operands, often with one operand also serving as destination.

entities.name: Three-operand instruction form
entities.description: Two sources and a separate destination.

entities.name: Four-operand instruction form
entities.description: Some operations encode a destination and three source inputs.

entities.name: Register pressure
entities.description: Demand for simultaneously live values relative to available registers.

entities.name: Register spilling
entities.description: Stores register values to stack or memory when register allocation capacity is exceeded.

entities.name: Data movement
entities.description: Transfers values between registers, memory, constants, stack, or architectural state.

entities.name: Load
entities.description: Reads a value from memory or an addressable source.

entities.name: Store
entities.description: Writes a value to memory or an addressable destination.

entities.name: Move
entities.description: Copies a value between operands while normally preserving the source.

entities.name: Input/output instruction
entities.description: Accesses architecturally defined device or I/O spaces where supported.

entities.name: Integer arithmetic
entities.description: Integer add, subtract, multiply, divide, increment, decrement, and related operations.

entities.name: Floating-point arithmetic
entities.description: Arithmetic over floating-point formats with defined rounding and exceptional behavior.

entities.name: Bitwise logic
entities.description: AND, OR, XOR, NOT, and related bit-pattern operations.

entities.name: Shift and rotate
entities.description: Shifts or rotates bit patterns under defined width and count rules.

entities.name: Compare and test
entities.description: Compares values or tests bits, often updating condition state.

entities.name: Branch
entities.description: Changes the next instruction address.

entities.name: Conditional branch
entities.description: Changes control flow when a condition or predicate is satisfied.

entities.name: Indirect branch
entities.description: Obtains a control-flow target from a register, memory operand, or computed value.

entities.name: Call
entities.description: Transfers control to a procedure and preserves return information.

entities.name: Return
entities.description: Resumes execution at a saved return location.

entities.name: Trap / software interrupt
entities.description: Requests a controlled exception or software-service transition.

entities.name: Atomic read-modify-write
entities.description: Performs an indivisible memory update, such as CAS or fetch-and-add.

entities.name: Load-linked / store-conditional
entities.description: Conditional update pattern used to build synchronization primitives.

entities.name: Fence / memory barrier
entities.description: Constrains ordering or visibility of memory operations.

entities.name: Vector / SIMD
entities.description: Applies an operation to multiple packed values or vector lanes.

entities.name: DSP / multiply-accumulate
entities.description: Signal-processing operation such as multiply-accumulate, often with specialized data paths.

entities.name: String operation
entities.description: Repeated or bulk operations over data sequences.

entities.name: Block transfer
entities.description: Transfers multiple registers or a block of memory.

entities.name: Decimal / BCD arithmetic
entities.description: Operations on decimal-coded representations.

entities.name: Cryptographic instruction
entities.description: Accelerates cryptographic transformations such as AES rounds or polynomial operations.

entities.name: Bit manipulation
entities.description: Bit extraction, deposit, population count, leading/trailing zero count, and related operations.

entities.name: Cache and prefetch control
entities.description: Hints or operations affecting cache, prefetch, or cache maintenance.

entities.name: System / privileged instruction
entities.description: Controls processor state, protection, translation, interrupts, or privileged facilities.

entities.name: Coprocessor instruction
entities.description: Transfers data to or invokes an associated specialized execution facility.

entities.name: Vector reduction
entities.description: Combines vector lanes into scalar or reduced results.

entities.name: Predicate operation
entities.description: Creates, combines, or consumes predicate state.

entities.name: Atomic memory operation (AMO)
entities.description: Atomically reads and updates a memory location.

entities.name: Instruction format
entities.description: Layout of operation selectors, register fields, immediates, displacements, and other bits.

entities.name: Fixed-length encoding
entities.description: Instructions or an instruction subset use a fixed instruction length.

entities.name: Variable-length encoding
entities.description: Instruction size varies by operation or operand form.

entities.name: Mixed-length encoding
entities.description: ISA supports multiple instruction lengths or encoding modes.

entities.name: Prefix byte / prefix field
entities.description: Encoding element modifying operation, operand size, addressing, or semantics.

entities.name: Register field
entities.description: Bits identifying an architectural register.

entities.name: Immediate field
entities.description: Bits encoding a constant, displacement, mask, or inline value.

entities.name: Displacement field
entities.description: Encoded offset used in address calculation or branch targeting.

entities.name: Instruction alignment
entities.description: Alignment requirement or performance property for instruction addresses.

entities.name: Instruction boundary
entities.description: Boundary between adjacent encoded instructions.

entities.name: Endianness
entities.description: Byte-order convention for multi-byte values; instruction encoding rules may differ by ISA.

entities.name: Instruction length
entities.description: Number of bits or bytes occupied by an instruction.

entities.name: Code density
entities.description: Useful program behavior represented per byte of machine code.

entities.name: Compressed instruction encoding
entities.description: Shorter encodings for common operations, often improving code size.

entities.name: Predication
entities.description: Instruction effects occur only when a predicate is satisfied.

entities.name: Condition field
entities.description: Field selecting the condition under which an operation is active.

entities.name: Delay slot
entities.description: Instruction slot after a control transfer with architecture-defined execution behavior.

entities.name: Instruction fetch
entities.description: Retrieves instruction bytes from the memory hierarchy.

entities.name: Instruction decode
entities.description: Interprets instruction encoding and identifies operations and operands.

entities.name: Memory address space
entities.description: Set of addresses available under architectural addressing rules.

entities.name: Virtual memory
entities.description: Translation and protection abstraction mapping virtual addresses to physical memory or backing resources.

entities.name: Physical address
entities.description: Address identifying a location in physical memory or physical address space.

entities.name: Virtual address
entities.description: Address generated by software and translated according to architectural rules.

entities.name: Address translation
entities.description: Maps virtual addresses to physical addresses and applies permissions.

entities.name: Page table
entities.description: Structure describing virtual-to-physical mappings and permissions.

entities.name: TLB
entities.description: Translation lookaside buffer caching address-translation results.

entities.name: Memory protection
entities.description: Rules restricting access by privilege, permissions, domains, keys, or metadata.

entities.name: Alignment
entities.description: Requirement or performance property for access address alignment.

entities.name: Unaligned access
entities.description: Access not meeting a natural or specified alignment boundary.

entities.name: Memory-mapped I/O
entities.description: Device registers occupy addresses in the memory address space.

entities.name: Port-mapped I/O
entities.description: Device access uses a separate I/O address space where supported.

entities.name: Memory ordering
entities.description: Constraints on how memory operations may be observed by other agents.

entities.name: Sequential consistency
entities.description: Operations appear in one global order consistent with each agent's program order.

entities.name: Relaxed memory ordering
entities.description: Model permitting specified reorderings while defining synchronization constraints.

entities.name: Atomicity
entities.description: Guarantee that an operation appears indivisible to relevant observers.

entities.name: Cache coherence
entities.description: Rules and mechanisms keeping cached copies of a memory location coherent.

entities.name: Fence
entities.description: Instruction constraining ordering of memory operations.

entities.name: Compare-and-swap (CAS)
entities.description: Atomically replaces a value if it matches an expected value.

entities.name: Fetch-and-add
entities.description: Atomically adds to a memory location and returns a specified old or resulting value.

entities.name: Load-link/store-conditional (LL/SC)
entities.description: Conditional store succeeds only if a linked reservation remains valid.

entities.name: Reservation granule
entities.description: Granularity relevant to tracking LL/SC reservations.

entities.name: Exception model
entities.description: Rules for identifying, prioritizing, reporting, and handling execution events.

entities.name: Precise exception
entities.description: Presents state as if instructions before a defined boundary completed and later ones did not.

entities.name: Fault
entities.description: Synchronous event associated with an instruction that cannot complete normally.

entities.name: Trap
entities.description: Synchronous event often used for deliberate software transition or post-instruction notification.

entities.name: Abort
entities.description: Exception category for failures where normal completion or restart may not be possible.

entities.name: Interrupt vector
entities.description: Location or table entry routing control to a handler.

entities.name: Context switch
entities.description: Operating-system transition that preserves/restores required execution state.

entities.name: Privilege transition
entities.description: Controlled change between execution privilege levels.

entities.name: Virtualization extension
entities.description: Architectural facilities supporting guest execution and hypervisor control.

entities.name: Debug and trace facility
entities.description: Facilities for breakpoints, watchpoints, stepping, counters, and tracing.

entities.name: Instruction-level parallelism (ILP)
entities.description: Potential to execute independent instructions concurrently or overlap processing.

entities.name: Pipelining
entities.description: Overlaps different instruction-processing stages.

entities.name: Out-of-order execution
entities.description: Executes ready operations in an order different from program order while preserving architectural behavior.

entities.name: Superscalar execution
entities.description: Issues or completes multiple instructions per cycle.

entities.name: Branch prediction
entities.description: Predicts control-flow outcomes and targets.

entities.name: Speculative execution
entities.description: Performs work before it is certain to be needed.

entities.name: Architectural retirement
entities.description: Point where instruction effects become committed to architectural state in many modern processors.

entities.name: Power-performance-area trade-off
entities.description: Design choices balance power, speed, silicon area, verification, and cost.

entities.name: Hardwired control
entities.description: Control sequencing implemented mainly with fixed logic.

entities.name: Microcoded control
entities.description: Control sequencing implemented partly with internal microinstruction sequences.

entities.name: FPGA implementation
entities.description: ISA implementation using reconfigurable logic.

entities.name: Hardware implementation
entities.description: Physical processor logic implementing an ISA.

entities.name: Software implementation
entities.description: Interpreter, emulator, or translator implementing an ISA in software.

entities.name: Compatibility test suite
entities.description: Tests whether an implementation conforms to specified architectural behavior.

entities.name: Formal ISA model
entities.description: Mathematical or executable description of architectural state transitions.

entities.name: Differential testing
entities.description: Compares implementations or simulators on shared test programs.

entities.name: Compiler instruction selection
entities.description: Maps intermediate operations to instructions supported by the target ISA.

entities.name: Register allocation
entities.description: Assigns live values to architectural registers and inserts spills when needed.

entities.name: Instruction scheduling
entities.description: Orders instructions to respect dependencies and improve performance.

entities.name: Optimization for size
entities.description: Code generation objective emphasizing smaller executable size.

entities.name: Optimization for speed
entities.description: Code generation objective emphasizing execution performance.

entities.name: Harvard architecture
entities.description: Separate instruction and data memories or paths.

entities.name: Von Neumann architecture
entities.description: Unified instruction/data memory organization.

entities.name: Digital signal processor (DSP)
entities.description: Processor optimized for signal processing, often with MAC operations and high-throughput data access.

entities.name: Fused multiply-add (FMA)
entities.description: Computes multiplication plus addition with one rounding step under defined floating-point semantics.

entities.name: Saturation arithmetic
entities.description: Clamps overflowed results to representable extrema rather than wrapping or trapping.

entities.name: Rounding mode
entities.description: Rule selecting how an inexact floating-point result is rounded.

entities.name: Floating-point exception flags
entities.description: Architectural indicators for invalid, divide-by-zero, overflow, underflow, or inexact results.

entities.name: Instruction cache
entities.description: Cache holding instruction bytes; maintenance interfaces may be architectural.

entities.name: Prefetch
entities.description: Hint or operation requesting earlier retrieval of instructions or data.

entities.name: x86
entities.description: CISC-family ISA originating with Intel 8086 and evolving through IA-32 and x86-64.

entities.name: x86-64
entities.description: 64-bit x86 extension with wider registers and addressing capabilities.

entities.name: ARM architecture
entities.description: Arm ISA family spanning A-, R-, and M-profile designs and multiple execution states.

entities.name: AArch64
entities.description: 64-bit Arm execution state with its own encoding and register model.

entities.name: AArch32
entities.description: 32-bit Arm execution state.

entities.name: Thumb / T32
entities.description: Compact Arm encoding family with 16-bit and 32-bit instruction encodings.

entities.name: RISC-V
entities.description: Open ISA with base integer architecture and modular standard/custom extensions.

entities.name: MIPS
entities.description: RISC ISA family known for register-oriented instructions and multiple generations.

entities.name: Power ISA
entities.description: ISA used by Power-family processors with scalar and vector extensions.

entities.name: SPARC
entities.description: RISC ISA family including register-window designs in several versions.

entities.name: IBM z/Architecture
entities.description: Mainframe ISA with compatibility history, conditional operations, and extensive system facilities.

entities.name: AVR
entities.description: 8-bit microcontroller ISA family.

entities.name: MSP430
entities.description: 16-bit low-power microcontroller ISA family.
Historical 8-bit accumulator-centric ISA.

entities.name: Z80
entities.description: Historical 8-bit ISA with registers, flags, and rich control-flow operations.

entities.name: VAX
entities.description: Historical CISC architecture with rich addressing and elaborate instructions.

entities.name: IBM System/360 architecture
entities.description: Compatibility-oriented architecture family separating programming model from implementation trade-offs.

entities.name: Java Virtual Machine (JVM) instruction set
entities.description: Stack-oriented bytecode instruction set interpreted or compiled by JVM implementations.

entities.name: Common Intermediate Language (CIL)
entities.description: Stack-based virtual instruction set used by the .NET runtime ecosystem.

entities.name: Smalltalk bytecode
entities.description: Virtual-machine instruction representation used by Smalltalk implementations.

entities.name: MMX
entities.description: Historical x86 packed-integer SIMD extension.

entities.name: SSE
entities.description: x86 SIMD extension family.

entities.name: AVX
entities.description: x86 vector extension family with wider registers and instruction forms.

entities.name: AVX-512
entities.description: x86 extension family with 512-bit vector facilities and mask capabilities on supporting processors.

entities.name: AES-NI
entities.description: x86 instructions accelerating AES transformations.

entities.name: AltiVec / VMX
entities.description: Power-family vector extension.

entities.name: ARM NEON
entities.description: Arm SIMD extension for packed integer and floating-point workloads.

entities.name: RISC-V Vector extension
entities.description: Scalable vector extension with vector length and vector configuration state.

entities.name: RISC-V Atomic extension
entities.description: RISC-V extension defining atomic memory operations.

entities.name: RISC-V Compressed extension
entities.description: RISC-V compact instruction encoding extension commonly called C.

entities.name: x86 VMX
entities.description: Intel x86 virtualization extension for guest execution and VM control.

entities.name: AMD-V / SVM
entities.description: AMD x86 virtualization facilities for guest execution and hypervisor control.

entities.name: IBM 3090 Vector Facility
entities.description: Historical vector processing facility for IBM 3090 systems.

entities.name: Intel 8087
entities.description: Floating-point coprocessor associated with early x86 systems.

entities.name: Transmeta code-morphing
entities.description: Approach translating x86 streams onto an internal VLIW execution engine.

entities.name: Fred Brooks
entities.description: Computer architect associated with articulating architecture versus implementation during IBM System/360 work.

entities.name: IBM System/360 compatibility objective
entities.description: Objective of a compatible architecture spanning processors with different cost and performance points.

entities.name: RISC research
entities.description: Research movement exploring simpler instruction sets, compiler cooperation, and efficient implementation.

entities.name: CISC design tradition
entities.description: Design tradition favoring rich instructions, operand forms, and addressing capabilities.

entities.name: Instruction atomicity
entities.description: Whether an instruction appears indivisible architecturally; distinct from atomic memory operations.

entities.name: Restartability
entities.description: Whether a faulted or interrupted instruction can safely resume from a defined state.

entities.name: Architectural register aliasing
entities.description: Different names or widths refer to overlapping architectural register state.

entities.name: Register window
entities.description: Organization exposing overlapping register sets across procedure calls.

entities.name: Condition-code architecture
entities.description: Design where operations update shared status flags used by later instructions.

entities.name: Predicate-register architecture
entities.description: Design using explicit predicate registers to control or mask effects.

entities.name: SIMD lane
entities.description: One element position within a packed vector operation.

entities.name: Vector length
entities.description: Number of active vector elements, fixed or configurable by ISA.

entities.name: Vector mask
entities.description: Predicate state controlling which vector lanes participate.

entities.name: Address generation unit (AGU)
entities.description: Implementation resource calculating effective addresses.

entities.name: Instruction latency
entities.description: Time from input availability to result availability under a stated implementation convention.

entities.name: Instruction throughput
entities.description: Sustainable rate of executing an operation or instruction class.

entities.name: Architectural compatibility level
entities.description: Baseline and extension level software may target for compatibility.

entities.name: Custom instruction extension
entities.description: Nonstandard or implementation-specific instructions requiring toolchain/runtime coordination.

entities.name: ISA specification
entities.description: Normative description of encodings, semantics, state, exceptions, and compatibility rules.

entities.name: Assembler
entities.description: Translates assembly statements into machine code and object records.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Combines object files, resolves symbols, and produces executable/shared objects.

entities.name: Compiler
entities.description: Translates high-level or intermediate representation into code targeting an ISA and ABI.

entities.name: Object file format
entities.description: Container for machine code, data, symbols, relocations, and metadata.

entities.name: Relocation
entities.description: Record or operation describing how an address-dependent field is adjusted by linker or loader.

entities.name: Calling convention
entities.description: Rules for argument passing, return values, register preservation, and stack usage.

entities.name: Exception handler
entities.description: Code entered to respond to an exception or interrupt.

entities.name: Operating system
entities.description: System software managing resources and using privileged facilities.

entities.name: Hypervisor
entities.description: Software managing virtual machines and using virtualization facilities.

entities.name: Application binary
entities.description: Executable machine-code program built for an ISA and platform ABI.

entities.name: Instruction legality
entities.description: Whether a bit pattern is valid under the active ISA, mode, and feature set.

entities.name: Feature-dependent encoding
entities.description: Encoding whose meaning or legality depends on enabled extensions or execution mode.

entities.name: Execution mode
entities.description: Mode changing instruction availability, state interpretation, or execution rules.

entities.name: Privilege-sensitive instruction
entities.description: Instruction whose availability/effect depends on privilege or configuration.

entities.name: Power management instruction
entities.description: Operation or hint for idle, wait, low-power, or power-state behavior.

entities.name: Timer and counter instruction
entities.description: Accesses architecturally defined timers, counters, or performance-monitoring state.

entities.name: Performance monitoring counter
entities.description: Counter exposed for measuring events, with access and event definitions varying by ISA.

entities.name: Security extension
entities.description: Architectural facilities for isolation, cryptography, memory tagging, or control-flow integrity.

entities.name: Control-flow integrity
entities.description: Mechanisms constraining indirect control flow or return behavior.

entities.name: Memory tagging
entities.description: Associates tags with pointers or memory granules to help detect invalid accesses.

entities.name: Pointer authentication
entities.description: Authenticates pointers or return addresses where supported.

entities.name: Memory encryption
entities.description: Protects memory contents against selected threat models using architecture/platform mechanisms.

relationships.description: Specifies or supports architectural data representations.
May define privilege levels and protected state.
ABI includes ISA conventions plus platform and OS contracts.
ISA is the software-visible contract; microarchitecture is its implementation.
Hardware and software systems realize the contract.
Conforming implementations can execute compatible binaries when feature and platform requirements match.
Architectures evolve through added instructions and state.
Software needs to discover optional feature support.
Some implementations decompose instructions into internal operations.
Execution resources realize operations while preserving architectural behavior.
Interpreter decodes and performs instruction effects.
Runtime translation converts code between execution representations.
Runtime may compile bytecode to native code.
Executable compatibility also depends on ABI, OS, and runtime.
CISC is one ISA design classification.
RISC is one ISA design classification.
VLIW groups multiple operations into wide instruction words.
EPIC exposes parallelism and compiler scheduling.
MISC uses a minimal instruction set.
OISC is a theoretical one-instruction model.
The design terms describe related wide-instruction approaches.
Both expose parallelism and shift scheduling toward software.
Many RISC ISAs separate memory access from ALU operations.
Stack arithmetic often has no explicit operands.
Separate source and destination registers are common.
Some TTA designs encode transport rather than a conventional opcode.
Some forms encode destination and three sources.
Compiler maps live values to registers.
Instruction selection maps operations to target instructions.
